List and match once more</b><br>Only when Code is running: activate Code, then run<br>steps 1 to 3 once more. macOS hides the windows of<br>backgrounded apps from System Events; activating<br>re-materializes the list (dashkit#9)." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="104" width="440" x="400" y="989" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="open" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=8;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontColor=#1a1a1a;fontSize=13;fontFamily=Helvetica;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacing=8;" value="<b>6. Open a genuinely new window</b><br>code -n &lt;path&gt;. Never code -r, never bare code<br>&lt;path&gt; (see note). Focus the matched window</b><br>Activate VS Code, then AXRaise<br>the exact window whose title<br>matched. Identification and focus<br>stay bound to the same window:<br>nothing re-matches in between." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="114" width="280" x="60" y="846" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="note1" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=8;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#666666;fontColor=#1a1a1a;fontSize=11;fontFamily=Helvetica;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacing=8;dashed=1;dashPattern=4 3;" value="<b>Why window titles?</b><br>VS Code has no API that lists which folder<br>each window has open. The dotfiles set<br>window.title to the opened folder’s full<br>path, a spaced em dash, then the branch.<br>The path before the first separator is the<br>identity." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="330" x="900" y="254" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="note2" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=8;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#666666;fontColor=#1a1a1a;fontSize=11;fontFamily=Helvetica;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacing=8;dashed=1;dashPattern=4 3;" value="<b>Why three match stages?</b><br>Exact alone misses two real cases. The<br>given path can sit below the window’s<br>folder (an ancestor is unreachable by<br>prefix matching, so git resolves the root).<br>Or the window can sit inside the given path<br>(a monorepo package opened as its own<br>window)." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="135" width="330" x="900" y="661" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="note3" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=8;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#666666;fontColor=#1a1a1a;fontSize=11;fontFamily=Helvetica;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacing=8;dashed=1;dashPattern=4 3;" value="<b>Why the second listing?</b><br>macOS culls the accessibility tree of<br>backgrounded apps: a running Code can<br>report zero windows. The running flag keeps<br>“Code closed” (a definitive empty answer)<br>apart from “running but nothing listed”<br>(maybe a cull)." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="330" x="900" y="989" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="note4" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=8;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#666666;fontColor=#1a1a1a;fontSize=11;fontFamily=Helvetica;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacing=8;dashed=1;dashPattern=4 3;" value="<b>Why code -n, and never code -r?</b><br>code -r focuses the right window on an<br>exact folder hit, but on a miss it loads<br>the folder into the last active window: a<br>hijack (microsoft/vscode#121926, #216602,<br>#215749). Bare code &lt;path&gt; behaves only<br>while window.openFoldersInNewWindow stays<br>at its default; -n pins the outcome and<br>keeps the CLI out of the matching business." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry div.div:
canopy
Jump to the window that runs the
selected agent. Hands over the
agent’s cwd as-is, which can be a
monorepo subdir.

div.div:
understory
Enter on a worktree row: open or
focus that worktree’s VS Code
window.

div.div:
coppice (Python twin)
Read only: “would deleting this
worktree strand a window?” Shares the
listing and parsing, then matches
strictly: the worktree itself or a
folder inside it.

div.div:
1. List windows
One osascript call: System Events, process Code,
name of every window. The same call also returns
whether Code is running at all.

div.div:
2. Parse titles to paths
Split each title on the first “ — ”, expand a
leading ~, keep absolute paths only. The branch
part is never matched, so phantom branch false
positives are impossible by construction.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 426px; height: 1px; padding-top: 739px; margin-left: 407px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #1a1a1a;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#1a1a1a, #d7d7d7); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
3. Match, strongest signal first
(1) exact: window path = the given path. (2)
work-tree root: window path = git rev-parse
--show-toplevel of the given path, for when the
given path is a subdir of the checkout. (3)
nested: window path sits inside the given path, on
an element boundary (/wt-a must not match
/wt-a-b).

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 206px; height: 1px; padding-top: 903px; margin-left: 517px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #1a1a1a;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#1a1a1a, #d7d7d7); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 426px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1041px; margin-left: 407px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #1a1a1a;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#1a1a1a, #d7d7d7); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
5. List and match once more
Only when Code is running: activate Code, then run
steps 1 to 3 once more. macOS hides the windows of
backgrounded apps from System Events; activating
re-materializes the list (dashkit#9).

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 426px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1189px; margin-left: 407px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #1a1a1a;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#1a1a1a, #d7d7d7); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
6. Open a genuinely new window
code -n <path>. Never code -r, never bare code
<path> (see note). If the code CLI is missing:
open -a fallback, which targets only the app, not
a window.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(248, 206, 204), rgb(81, 45, 43)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(184, 84, 80), rgb(215, 129, 126));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 266px; height: 1px; padding-top: 427px; margin-left: 67px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #1a1a1a;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#1a1a1a, #d7d7d7); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Stop with an actionable error
Most likely cause: the macOS
Automation permission for System
Events is not granted. Never open
blind: that could stack the
duplicate window this library
exists to prevent.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 266px; height: 1px; padding-top: 903px; margin-left: 67px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #1a1a1a;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#1a1a1a, #d7d7d7); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
4. Focus the matched window
Activate VS Code, then AXRaise
the exact window whose title
matched. Identification and focus
stay bound to the same window:
nothing re-matches in between.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 316px; height: 1px; padding-top: 314px; margin-left: 907px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #1a1a1a;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#1a1a1a, #d7d7d7); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Why window titles?
VS Code has no API that lists which folder
each window has open. The dotfiles set
window.title to the opened folder’s full
path, a spaced em dash, then the branch.
The path before the first separator is the
identity.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 316px; height: 1px; padding-top: 729px; margin-left: 907px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #1a1a1a;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#1a1a1a, #d7d7d7); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Why three match stages?
Exact alone misses two real cases. The
given path can sit below the window’s
folder (an ancestor is unreachable by
prefix matching, so git resolves the root).
Or the window can sit inside the given path
(a monorepo package opened as its own
window).

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 316px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1049px; margin-left: 907px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #1a1a1a;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#1a1a1a, #d7d7d7); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Why the second listing?
macOS culls the accessibility tree of
backgrounded apps: a running Code can
report zero windows. The running flag keeps
“Code closed” (a definitive empty answer)
apart from “running but nothing listed”
(maybe a cull).

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 316px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1212px; margin-left: 907px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #1a1a1a;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#1a1a1a, #d7d7d7); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Why code -n, and never code -r?
code -r focuses the right window on an
exact folder hit, but on a miss it loads
the folder into the last active window: a
hijack (microsoft/vscode#121926, #216602,
#215749). Bare code <path> behaves only
while window.openFoldersInNewWindow stays
at its default; -n pins the outcome and
keeps the CLI out of the matching business.
